learn.pageTitle: Riichi Mahjong Pinfu Scoring: 20 Fu Tsumo, 30 Fu Ron
learn.pageDescription: How to score pinfu in riichi mahjong: why there are only two patterns, 20 fu by tsumo and 30 fu by ron, with a table of scores for each han to memorize.
learn.twoPatternsTitle: Pinfu has two patterns: 20 fu or 30 fu
learn.twoPatternsBody1:
Tanyao (all simples) and [[pinfu|pinfu]] are two of the most common yaku in mahjong.
Here we start by learning how to score pinfu.
learn.twoPatternsBody2: Pinfu splits broadly into two cases: 20 fu for a [[tsumo|tsumo]] win and 30 fu for a [[ron|ron]] win.
learn.twoPatternsBody3: With tanyao and other yaku you also have to consider cases such as 40 fu or 50 fu, but pinfu has only two patterns, so it is easy.
learn.columnBody:
Kiriage mangan is the rule that rounds 30 fu 4 han (7,700 points for a non-dealer, 11,600 for the dealer) up to mangan (8,000 for a non-dealer, 12,000 for the dealer).

Whether it is used depends on the house rules; the table above follows the standard rule without rounding up.

Check which rule is in use before you play.
learn.columnSettingsNote: * In this app you can switch in <settingsLink>Settings</settingsLink> whether practice and the scoring table use kiriage mangan
learn.whyBody1:
20 fu applies only to a pinfu tsumo.
You may wonder: "The [[futei|base fu]] is 20 fu, and a tsumo adds 2 fu, so shouldn't it count as 30 fu?" It is better to simply accept that this is how it works.
learn.whyBody2: A ron, on the other hand, is 30 fu. A tsumo does not get [[tsumo-fu|tsumo fu]], but a ron gets the [[menzen-ron-kafu|closed ron bonus]] and becomes 30 fu. Here too, we recommend not thinking too hard and simply accepting it.
learn.compositeTitle: Still 20 fu or 30 fu with other yaku
learn.compositeBody1: Pinfu can combine with yaku such as tanyao and sanshoku (mixed triple sequence), but even then the rule holds: it is always either 20 fu or 30 fu.
learn.compositeBody2: Pinfu means a "flat win". By its nature, all of its [[mentsu|sets]] are [[shuntsu|sequences]], so no fu are added for sets, and since it needs a [[ryanmen|two-sided wait]] (ryanmen), it gets no fu for the [[machi|wait]] either. The [[jantou|pair]] must not be [[yakuhai|yakuhai]], so there are no fu for the pair.
learn.compositeBody3: Once the han reach [[mangan|mangan]] or more, you no longer need to think about 20 fu or 30 fu at all.
